BugFX-055
SM-API-11 (added by FX-054) went red on CI on all three attempts, "an existing slot is taken", while it was green on Windows.
2026-10-26

SM-API-11 (added by FX-054) went red on CI on all three attempts, "an existing slot is taken", while it was green on Windows. Cause: the case stood in an empty directory for a held slot, and POSIX rename replaces an empty destination directory instead of failing, so on Linux the second rename won. A real slot is never empty — it holds owner.json — and onto a full directory Linux fails with ENOTEMPTY (probed in a node:22-alpine container: empty destination replaced, full destination ENOTEMPTY), so the pool itself was right and the case was wrong. Fixed: both scratch directories hold an owner.json, as a real slot does. Not caught locally because acceptance runs on Windows only; CI is the Linux run. Path: short, below the threshold

Found by: CI run 40326115185 on main

BugFX-054
SM-API-09 went red once in pnpm verify with "the scratch slot pool-05 was already taken" in a scratch pool no other test could reach, and green onâ€¦
2026-10-26

SM-API-09 went red once in pnpm verify with "the scratch slot pool-05 was already taken" in a scratch pool no other test could reach, and green on the rerun. Cause: a pool claim is an atomic rename (ADR-0037), and renameOrFalse in e2e/fixtures/suite.ts read every failed rename as "taken"; on Windows EPERM is both the loser's code and the code of a directory briefly held by an indexer or antivirus scan, so a free slot could be reported taken. In a live claim that only skipped a slot; in the scratch setup it failed the case. Fixed: a failure is "taken" only while the destination exists; with no destination it is transient and retried for up to 1 s. New case SM-API-11 drives renameOrFalse with a rename that throws EPERM once (won) and onto an existing slot (taken, not retried); it went red with the old semantics restored, green with the fix. The cause is inferred, not reproduced on demand: the observed failure could not be provoked, so the case pins the mechanism rather than the incident. Path: short, below the threshold

Found by: pnpm verify during CH-040 acceptance; green on the rerun

BugFX-052
The web project went red in pnpm verify at random: the failing cases moved between runs (AL-FN-02/03/04/08, ACC-FN-02/04/05/06, MF-FN-07/09/12) andâ€¦
2026-10-16

The web project went red in pnpm verify at random: the failing cases moved between runs (AL-FN-02/03/04/08, ACC-FN-02/04/05/06, MF-FN-07/09/12) and were green standalone. Cause: next dev (Next 16.3.8, Turbopack) compiles a route on its first request, and with up to 14 workers the first requests to never-compiled routes all arrived at once under the suite's own CPU contention. Two failures followed: Next answered its own 13,156-byte HTML 404 on the files route handler before our handler ran, and the 404 stuck for the life of that process (a lone cold request returned 200); and the first logins paid for compilation inside the 10 s expect.timeout. Fixed: a serial globalSetup warm-up (e2e/fixtures/warm-up.ts, wired in playwright.config.ts) that runs after both webServer entries answer, logs in through the real form, visits each route of apps/web once and aborts naming the route on a 404 or an unexpected status; no timeout, workers or fullyParallel change. Reproduction was a written CPU-load procedure (7 busy-loops, pnpm e2e --project=web), red 3 of 5 on the old code, with no new case ID; fix green 5 of 5 under the same load; control experiment (the globalSetup line disabled) green, green, red on run 3 (AL-FN-13 stayed on /auth/login for 10 s), then restored. Acceptance: three consecutive green pnpm verify (91 s, 97 s, 99 s, 173 passed each). Corpus: no fact moves (stated by the designer and the planner). Closes BL-058. Path: full (docs/plans/web-e2e-flake)

Found by: pnpm verify during the unrelated acceptance runs of clean-architecture-pilot and meetings-clean-architecture; reproduced by the CPU-load procedure in docs/plans/web-e2e-flake/research/probes.md, because no test covered concurrent first compiles under next dev

ACC-FN-03 (the login form in its error state, axe, WCAG 2.1 AA) went red on main in CI (run 38429549429, also 37127168216, and 2 of 3 attempts of 37930853945), and the cause was two things at once plus a test that could not see it. (1) HeroUI's default --danger (#ff383c) measures 3.56:1 on white and 3.25:1 on the page canvas, below the 4.5:1 AA bar, on the text-danger role="alert" paragraphs of the login, create-meeting and upload forms; FX-039 had overridden --accent only, so this was the same class arriving without a diff (ADR-0023). (2) HeroUI's default --accent-hover (#7766e8) puts the primary button's hover state at 4.22:1 under --snow, also below AA. (3) ACC-FN-03 waited on a bare getByRole('alert'), which Next's route announcer also matches: depending on when the announcer mounted, the locator either failed on strict mode or was satisfied before the form's error paragraph existed, so the scan ran on a DOM without the error and passed vacuously (the FIX-S2 probe: 3 of 5 red on the bare wait, 5 of 5 on the error text). Every green run of the case since it was added on 2026-10-01 (38d86d4; green runs since 2026-10-02) was therefore vacuous, and retries turned one red into "1 flaky"; the corpus gate in ADR-0026 named ACC-FN-01, which never renders an error. Fixed by ADR-0033: :root in apps/web/src/app/globals.css gains --danger: oklch(0.55 0.21 25.74) (5.42:1 on white, 4.93:1 on the canvas) and --accent-hover: oklch(0.5 0.21 285) (6.38:1 under --snow); ACC-FN-03 now waits on the main-scoped alert and its error text, and the two error states it never reached are covered by the new ACC-FN-05 (create-meeting) and ACC-FN-06 (upload); the old gate fact is retired into the register of ADR-0026, successor FACT-3691 (ADR-0022), and the false claim that a bare locator fails loudly in every error case is corrected in e2e/README.md and the comment of auth-login.functional.spec.ts and its cases file. Control experiment (pnpm e2e --project=web --grep "ACC-FN-0[356]" --repeat-each=5 --workers=1): leg 1, both overrides reverted: 15/15 red at the violations assertion (color-contrast 3.56:1 on white in 10, 3.25:1 on the canvas in 5, and the 4.22:1 button pair logged in 5 runs); leg 2, --accent-hover only reverted: 5/15 red, all ACC-FN-03 (the login button, 4.22:1, #fcfcfc on #7766e8), ACC-FN-05 and ACC-FN-06 green; with both overrides in place 15/15 green. 2026-10-06

This project's own CVE override pulled multer@2.4.0 as the floor satisfying @nestjs/platform-express's range; 2.4.0 renamed its LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE error message, and @nestjs/platform-express matches that string by exact equality to convert it into Nest's documented 400. The mismatch meant the conversion never fired and an upload under the wrong field name answered Nest's default 500 instead of the contracted {"message":"Unexpected field - <name>","statusCode":400}. Fixed by pinning multer to exactly 2.3.0 in pnpm-workspace.yaml (not left open as >=2.3.0) — the patched floor that still carries the string @nestjs/platform-express@12.0.1 matches against

BugFX-042
Next's Server Action FormData decoder substitutes the literal filename 'blob' for any part submitted with filename="" — the WHATWG default for anâ€¦
2026-10-06

Next's Server Action FormData decoder substitutes the literal filename 'blob' for any part submitted with filename="" — the WHATWG default for an unnamed Blob — before our code ever sees it. 'blob' passes the filename rule's own shape check, so submitting the upload form with no file chosen reached the 415 (unsupported content type) branch instead of the documented 400 file is required, silently changing which message the user saw for invariant 15's empty-selection case

Found by: MF-FN-15, the browser-level empty-selection scenario — invisible to any API-level case, since the substitution happens inside the browser's own FormData encoding before the request leaves the client

BugFX-041
The meeting-file download controller built Content-Disposition by interpolating the stored filename directly.
2026-10-06

The meeting-file download controller built Content-Disposition by interpolating the stored filename directly. Two of SEC-API-11's five hostile seeded rows carry a bare CR/LF; the only thing between that stored byte sequence and a split HTTP response was Node's own setHeader validator throwing — a defence this code did not own — and both rows answered 500 instead of the contracted 200. Fixed by building the header per RFC 6266's filename/filename* pairing instead of interpolating (buildContentDisposition, meeting-files.rules.ts); all five hostile rows and the benign one now answer 200 with both parameters correctly encoded, and two non-security symptoms (déjà-vu.png mis-decoded as latin-1, report".txt truncating at the quote) close as a side effect of the same fix

Found by: SEC-API-11, written specifically against the write path that bypasses the controller — the seed inserts the five hostile filenames straight through Prisma, so the download is exercised on attacker-controlled data the upload path never had to validate

2026-10-03

text-foreground-500 (seven occurrences) and border-default-200 (two) in apps/web were HeroUI v2 token names: v3 defines --muted and --border with no numeric scale, so both classes compile to no CSS at all. Secondary text rendered at full foreground instead of muted, and the two borders fell back to currentColor instead of the themed border colour. Fixed by the token swap to text-muted / border-border as part of BL-031's rollout (closes BL-032). No red test was constructible for this defect at the functional level: the dead class renders secondary text at _full_ foreground, which _increases_ contrast rather than reducing it — so axe passes, every functional case passes and the diff looks clean. It survived a code review, an accessibility scan and 28 functional cases for exactly that reason

BL-069 e2e Intermittent read ECONNRESET in the web project.

Intermittent read ECONNRESET in the web project. Under the FX-052 load procedure without the warm-up, 3 of 20 pnpm e2e --project=web runs failed with read ECONNRESET on Playwright APIRequestContext calls from the test process to Nest :3101 (POST /auth/login in loginPoolUser; GET /meetings?limit=50 in fetchMeetingsPage); the control with the old warm-up was 10/10 green. The difference is not significant (Fisher about 0.2). A cause investigation could not reproduce it: Nest runs Node's default keepAliveTimeout of 5 s and Playwright's agent uses keepAlive: true, so stale keep-alive socket reuse is a candidate, but it is not shown. Suggested next step: capture NODE_DEBUG=http,net or socket.reusedSocket on failure in a loaded run, or run an arm with a raised keepAliveTimeout or Connection: close. Above the bugfix-pipeline §4 threshold (cause not found in about fifteen minutes), so it needs its own change. Evidence: probe P14, docs/plans/e2e-test-architecture/research/probes.md

2026-10-26 Fix FX-055 SM-API-11 (added by FX-054) went red on CI on all three attempts, "an existing slot is taken", while it was green on Windows.

SM-API-11 (added by FX-054) went red on CI on all three attempts, "an existing slot is taken", while it was green on Windows. Cause: the case stood in an empty directory for a held slot, and POSIX rename replaces an empty destination directory instead of failing, so on Linux the second rename won. A real slot is never empty — it holds owner.json — and onto a full directory Linux fails with ENOTEMPTY (probed in a node:22-alpine container: empty destination replaced, full destination ENOTEMPTY), so the pool itself was right and the case was wrong. Fixed: both scratch directories hold an owner.json, as a real slot does. Not caught locally because acceptance runs on Windows only; CI is the Linux run. Path: short, below the threshold

Found by: CI run 40326115185 on main

Commit: 2475216

2026-10-26 Fix FX-054 SM-API-09 went red once in pnpm verify with "the scratch slot pool-05 was already taken" in a scratch pool no other test could reach, and green onâ€¦

SM-API-09 went red once in pnpm verify with "the scratch slot pool-05 was already taken" in a scratch pool no other test could reach, and green on the rerun. Cause: a pool claim is an atomic rename (ADR-0037), and renameOrFalse in e2e/fixtures/suite.ts read every failed rename as "taken"; on Windows EPERM is both the loser's code and the code of a directory briefly held by an indexer or antivirus scan, so a free slot could be reported taken. In a live claim that only skipped a slot; in the scratch setup it failed the case. Fixed: a failure is "taken" only while the destination exists; with no destination it is transient and retried for up to 1 s. New case SM-API-11 drives renameOrFalse with a rename that throws EPERM once (won) and onto an existing slot (taken, not retried); it went red with the old semantics restored, green with the fix. The cause is inferred, not reproduced on demand: the observed failure could not be provoked, so the case pins the mechanism rather than the incident. Path: short, below the threshold

Found by: pnpm verify during CH-040 acceptance; green on the rerun

2026-10-16 Fix FX-052 The web project went red in pnpm verify at random: the failing cases moved between runs (AL-FN-02/03/04/08, ACC-FN-02/04/05/06, MF-FN-07/09/12) andâ€¦

The web project went red in pnpm verify at random: the failing cases moved between runs (AL-FN-02/03/04/08, ACC-FN-02/04/05/06, MF-FN-07/09/12) and were green standalone. Cause: next dev (Next 16.3.8, Turbopack) compiles a route on its first request, and with up to 14 workers the first requests to never-compiled routes all arrived at once under the suite's own CPU contention. Two failures followed: Next answered its own 13,156-byte HTML 404 on the files route handler before our handler ran, and the 404 stuck for the life of that process (a lone cold request returned 200); and the first logins paid for compilation inside the 10 s expect.timeout. Fixed: a serial globalSetup warm-up (e2e/fixtures/warm-up.ts, wired in playwright.config.ts) that runs after both webServer entries answer, logs in through the real form, visits each route of apps/web once and aborts naming the route on a 404 or an unexpected status; no timeout, workers or fullyParallel change. Reproduction was a written CPU-load procedure (7 busy-loops, pnpm e2e --project=web), red 3 of 5 on the old code, with no new case ID; fix green 5 of 5 under the same load; control experiment (the globalSetup line disabled) green, green, red on run 3 (AL-FN-13 stayed on /auth/login for 10 s), then restored. Acceptance: three consecutive green pnpm verify (91 s, 97 s, 99 s, 173 passed each). Corpus: no fact moves (stated by the designer and the planner). Closes BL-058. Path: full (docs/plans/web-e2e-flake)

2026-09-30 Process CH-024 The fact base gains a lifecycle and the pipeline is wired to it.

The fact base gains a lifecycle and the pipeline is wired to it. ADR-0022: a fact is appended and retired, never deleted and never rewritten in place under its own key. A changed fact is retired into its document's ## Retired facts register naming the key that supersedes it; one that stops being true with no replacement is withdrawn naming what withdrew it. The gap it closes: CH-023 stated that a key is never reused and a withdrawn fact retires its number, and nothing enforced either — a fact could be deleted outright, or its statement repointed at different words while every reference kept resolving, which is worse than deletion. docs/facts-lock.json pins all 547 keys with a SHA-256 of each statement, the shape skills-lock.json already uses; pnpm fact:lock writes it, pnpm fact:check compares offline. AR-API-15 catches a deleted or silently reworded fact, AR-API-16 a retirement naming no successor or a dead one, AR-API-17 drives both over an in-spec fixture because the corpus has no retirements yet and the rules would otherwise pass having parsed nothing. AR-API-14 gained a living/historical split: a living document must cite a _stated_ fact, while a change folder or profiling record may keep pointing at a retired one, because editing it would falsify the record. Wiring: all 23 roles and 11 of 14 skills, each a pointer plus its own part rather than a copy of the rule — the three left out are adapters to external sets. docs/process.md states that the corpus moves inside FEAT-S4 and adds no stage; the plan template gains section 3a. The parser now lives once in scripts/facts-parse.mjs, read by both the lock and the meta-test, and learned to skip fenced code blocks — found when this record's own illustrative register was parsed as five real facts

2026-09-29 Process CH-023 Every statement of fact in the architecture corpus now carries a FACT-NNNN key and names its source, and everything that is not a fact sits in aâ€¦

Every statement of fact in the architecture corpus now carries a FACT-NNNN key and names its source, and everything that is not a fact sits in a block opening > Rationale — not a fact. with no key (ADR-0021). 522 facts keyed across architecture.md, data-model.md, api-contract.md and all 21 records; keys are allocated from a block per document (0001/1000/2000/3000) by pnpm fact:next, never by hand. The gap it closes: the evidence rule — cite everything, conclude nothing — bound only the research stage (PR-API-06), while the durable documents that stage feeds had no such rule and no check; a measured fact and an inference drawn from it occupied the same sentence shape and were indistinguishable by a reader or by grep. Four checks, AR-API-11…AR-API-14: keys unique and inside their document's block, every keyed fact naming a source, no key defined inside a rationale block, and every FACT- reference in the repository resolving. AR-API-12 found four unsourced rows on its first run — three "adding an endpoint" steps and one change-the-data-model step under a Source: the checks named in each row header that named none. What it deliberately does not do: check that a fact is true — a key makes a statement addressable, review makes it right (ADR-0010). Half-checkable by construction: an agent's memory lives outside git, so the repository can verify that a key cited inside it exists but never that a memory entry cites a real one; a memory pointing at a retired key is caught when read, not when written. The ADRs changed in form only — no decision, date, status or rejected alternative was reworded

2026-09-29 Process CH-022 Third tuning round: the defect flow becomes self-standing instead of borrowing FEAT-S1…FEAT-S3 by reference.

Third tuning round: the defect flow becomes self-standing instead of borrowing FEAT-S1…FEAT-S3 by reference. Its own FIX-S8 research, FIX-S9 design and FIX-S10 plan, placed after impact rather than before reproduction — the threshold's first condition, "the cause was not found in about fifteen minutes", cannot be judged before the cause is looked for. FIX-S11 adds a profiling record above the threshold only. Zero review gates by design, against the feature flow's four; what stands in for them is mechanical and specific to this flow — the red test must fail on current code, and the control experiment reverts the fix and requires it red again. The short and full paths are named in the inventory instead of left to judgement. FIX-S5 splits between test-designer and the tester of the level; FIX-S7 drops lead, which has no Write — the same defect FX-034 fixed for the feature flow and missed here. The disputed-test rule now routes through escalation, and TEMPLATE-BUGFIX.md gains a place to mark tests expected to break, without which that rule fired on every red case. On the owner's amendment at the approval gate: a defect is not only a red test — the entry accepts one found in the running application, in the code, in an owner's report or during unrelated work; where nothing covers the area, a written repeatable procedure is reproduction evidence on equal footing; the red test there is new coverage rather than a repair; and the coverage gap itself is recorded in the FX- entry's "Found by" column, so it does not evaporate when the defect is fixed. No FIX cycle has run yet, so every effect is projected

Run 2: MF-FN-07 (expected 200, received 404 on the download route), MF-FN-09 ("first hop, from the download route" expected 307 received 404), MF-FN-12 (expected empty body, received Next's 13,156-byte HTML 404) — the route handler apps/web/src/app/meetings/[id]/files/[fileId]/route.ts answered Next's own HTML 404 on its first next dev compile (next.js: 2.5s). Run 3: AL-FN-02 (toHaveURL / timed out at 10 s, stayed on /auth/login) and AL-FN-04 (login alert not visible within 10 s). The same cases were green standalone and in run 4 (exit 0, 171 passed); apps/web and auth were untouched by the change. Three suite runs lost (84 s, 138 s and 155 s). Recurred on meetings-clean-architecture (FT-009), verify run 2 of 2026-10-16 (111 s): AL-FN-02, toHaveURL('/') stayed on /auth/login after 10 s (test 14.7 s), green in runs 1 and 3, no apps/web or auth file touched. Cause not found: first-compile latency of a route under next dev and load from fullyParallel are candidates, neither confirmed

BL-024closed by FX-046 (ADR-0031):runtime ids are now mtg-/fil- + randomUUID().

Closed by FX-046 (ADR-0031): runtime ids are now mtg-/fil- + randomUUID(). Was: two identifier formats coexisted. The identifier rule (FACT-1082) in docs/data-model.md mandates opaque strings with a type prefix (usr-, mtg-, fil-), never guessable by increment; meetings.service.ts and the upload handler both issue a bare randomUUID() at runtime, so the database holds both shapes and no seed id is a UUID. The meeting-files change added a third prefixed family (fil-) and ADR-0027's identifier consequence (FACT-3670) carried the divergence forward deliberately rather than settling it

BL-004closed by CH-031 — rejected, see RejectedWas: unblocked by FT-007, not closed: meeting-files gave the seed a database and the seed script now computes hashes rather than hard-coding them,â€¦

Closed by CH-031 — rejected, see Rejected. Was: unblocked by FT-007, not closed: meeting-files gave the seed a database and the seed script now computes hashes rather than hard-coding them, but plaintext-out-of-users.seed.ts itself was deliberately kept out of that change's scope (plan §0, "Conflicts with planned")

ProposalWhy rejected
Unit coverage for lib/dal.ts, proxy.ts, lib/actions/*The modules are server-only or Server Actions — Vitest cannot resolve them in principle. SEC-FN-04, SEC-FN-05, HD-FN-01, HD-FN-08 go through them. Extracting logic for a metric would make the code worse
React component tests in jsdomThe UI is covered by functional Playwright tests in a real browser; jsdom would give a second, less trustworthy copy of the same checks
Deleting docs/plans/plan-review-*.md (1416 lines)They record why decisions came out this way, including nine blockers that would otherwise look like unmotivated edits. Marked as archive — that is enough
Pluralizing the meeting counterThe Meetings total: N format and pluralization are mutually exclusive; pluralizing would break the HD-FN-03 locator. The helper was deleted along with cases HD-UT-13/HD-UT-14
Moving the seed's plaintext password out of users.seed.ts (BL-004)It cannot leave the repository, only move: e2e/fixtures/seed.ts must hold the same plaintext for every login case, and an environment variable would add setup to CI and every local run for no secrecy. The database already stores only scrypt hashes. The real risk — seeding a production database with these accounts — is closed instead by assertSeedAllowed (AL-UT-32, CH-031)
Mutation testingThe "prove the tests do not pass blindly" role is already filled by the mandatory control experiments, and they cost seconds against minutes of a full mutation run
A global fullyParallel: false to remove racesIt would slow the whole suite down for the sake of five mutating cases. The races are solved by dedicated owners, a serial block and relative counters
A state reset endpoint for testsA test back door in a production API. Isolation is achieved through data: dedicated owners for mutations
pnpm audit --audit-level=low in verifyIt would make any advisory in the dependency tree a blocker. The high threshold catches what actually needs a reaction
Removing one or more of the four FEAT review gates (P2, 2a-2d)Put to the owner at TUNE-G1 of the fourth round and declined: the gates stay until a second profiling record exists. Their own cost is 595,875 tokens, 17.1% of the one measured cycle, and across 36 FX- rows exactly one names a review gate — but a gate catches before a defect exists, so the ledger cannot see most of what it finds, and the one measured cycle credits them with two security cases, a vacuous guarantee, a cases doc describing the inverse of its own check and an unnamed fifth copy site. P1 (CH-025) takes the rework half of the cost without removing a gate
Dropping FEAT-S6 acceptance below a named size (P4)Declined at TUNE-G1 of the fourth round: P3 captures most of the same 286,179 tokens by removing the dispatch rather than the run, without removing a check that has found two ledger defects (FX-005, FX-030) plus FX-004 jointly — the second-best yield in the ledger — and without a new ADR superseding ADR-0014
Changing a role's model (P5)Declined at TUNE-G1 of the fourth round: the profiling records measure tokens, not price, so the saving is zero in the only unit the repository holds and the change is unfalsifiable. Revisit once a record carries the model and the tokens of every row, from which price is derivable
TUNE-S3 writing a profiling record for the tuning round (P8)Declined at TUNE-G1 of the fourth round: it is the cheapest kind of "add a step", which is what CH-004 is the ledger entry for. Four rounds have run with zero TUNE data points and that remains true
